title: Modern and Mexican: Mario Pani’s CUPA Housing Complex in Mexico City
text:
Modern and Mexican: Mario Pani’s CUPA Housing Complex in Mexico City

In 1947, Mexico's General Directorate of Civil Pensions commissioned young architect Mario Pani to design 200 houses for government employees on a recently acquired plot of land in Colonia del Valle, then a distant neighborhood on the outskirts of Mexico City. Rather than following the original guidelines, Pani proposed a 13-story housing complex with extensive green areas, communal spaces, and more than a thousand apartments. Drawing on Le Corbusier's functionalist principles, the architect created a project that opened in 1949 and would become a landmark in Latin American modern architecture.

title: The Cloud House / Peter Morris Architects
text:
The Cloud House / Peter Morris Architects

Architect Peter Morris reveals his most remarkable achievement to date: 'The Cloud House'. Drawing inspiration from the eccentric, Grade I-listed St Martin's Church opposite, and the castle-like Grade II-listed school next door, the property brings a touch of fairytale flamboyance to its north London surroundings. Its pale-pink exteriors, oversized arches, and duck-egg blue metalwork bring joyfulness and colour to the eclectic local architecture, with an interior featuring pale turquoise painted epoxy floors, pink and white marquee stripes on walls and ceilings, and an emerald green and white striped kitchen with pale pink Plykea worktops.

title: The Nordic Pavilion Explores Traditional Craft Through "Painted Matter" at the 2027 Venice Architecture Biennale
text:
The Nordic Pavilion Explores Traditional Craft Through "Painted Matter" at the 2027 Venice Architecture Biennale

The National Museum of Norway has announced Painted Matter as the title of Norway's contribution to the 20th International Architecture Exhibition of the Venice Biennale, scheduled to take place from May 8 to November 21, 2027. Developed by Oslo-based practice Kastler Skjeseth Architects, the exhibition will be presented at the Nordic Pavilion and will explore the role of traditional decorative painting techniques in contemporary architecture, with a focus on material use, architectural expression, and sustainability. The Nordic Pavilion, designed by Norwegian architect Sverre Fehn, is jointly owned by Norway, Sweden, and Finland. For the 2027 edition, the National Museum of Norway is responsible for organizing the Nordic contribution on behalf of Moderna Museet in Stockholm and the Architecture and Design Museum in Helsinki.

title: UN-Habitat and ICPAC Launch a Practical Guide to Help Cities Prepare for El Niño
text:
UN-Habitat and ICPAC Launch a Practical Guide to Help Cities Prepare for El Niño

El Niño is a natural climate pattern expected to peak from October 2026 through March 2027. It is characterized by a strong impact on global weather patterns, bringing floods, droughts, heat waves and storms to different regions. On November 5, 2026, the United Nations Human Settlements Programme (UN-Habitat) and the Climate Prediction and Applications Centre (ICPAC) of the Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) launched a short practical guide for city governments to help them prepare for the upcoming season. The guide offers considerations applicable to different climate regions, but it is framed by IGAD in the context of preparedness, anticipatory action and resilience in the Horn of Africa (Djibouti, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan and Uganda). Its aim is to offer actionable guidance to improve urban resilience, protect vulnerable communities and reduce the impacts of climate-related hazards.

text:
Miami Architecture City Guide: 22 Projects Shaping Tropical Density on the Atlantic Coast

Stretching along the Atlantic coast at the southern tip of Florida, Miami is often introduced through postcard views of beaches, palm trees, and glass towers facing the water. Yet, behind this familiar image lies a city shaped by migration, tourism, and real estate cycles, where architecture has repeatedly been used to project new identities and reinvent the urban landscape. From early resort hotels and the Art Deco façades of South Beach to experimental high-rises and cultural institutions on the bay, the built environment offers a way to read how Miami negotiates climate, economy, and everyday life.
